body:
This is just asking for troubles IMO and makes it harder to understand the code and available messages.

Just have an if/else if/else etc that calls the functions directly.

It's not a clean code, but it's an exact copy of existing code in all other debugger instances. I guess in this case, there's only one message function. Not sure what's better, keeping it consistent or more readable.

> It's not a clean code, but it's an exact copy of existing code in all other debugger instances. I guess in this case, there's only one message function. Not sure what's better, keeping it consistent or more readable.

It seems to come from #104895 .

I think it's okay to have all the handler as functions, but using functions pointers like that it's IMO **really bad** (and if you ask me, should be changed back to if/else).

It makes it really hard to know which messages you are parsing in each debugger.

You should be able to tell which messages are being parsed by just looking at the parse function.
I have changed specific case added in this PR to a simple `if`.
